source_text: Περὶ τοῦ μὴ συγχωρεῖν εἰς τὰ κοιμητήρια, ἢ εἰς τὰ λεγόμενα μαρτύρια πάντων τῶν αἱρετικῶν ἀπιέναι τοὺς τῆς ἐκκλησίας, εὐχῆς ἢ θεραπείας ἕνεκα· ἀλλὰ τοὺς τοιούτους, ἐὰν ὦσι πιστοί, ἀκοινωνήτους γίνεσθαι μέχρι τινός. Μετανοοῦντας δέ, καὶ ἐξομολουμένους, ἐσφάλθαι, παραδέχεσθαι. Ἐ ρ μ η ν ε ί α. Ὄχι μόνον οἱ αἱρετικοὶ δέν πρέπει νά ἐμβαίνουν εἰς τάς Ἐκκλησίας τῶν ὀρθοδόξων, ἀλλ’ οὐδὲ οἱ ἐκ τῆς Ἐκκλησίας, ἤτοι οἱ πιστοὶ λαϊκοὶ καὶ ὀρθόδοξοι πρέπει νά πηγαίνουν εἰς τὰ κοιμητήρια τῶν αἱρετικῶν, ὅπου τινὲς ὀνομαστοὶ παρὰ τοῖς αἱρετικοῖς ἐνταφιάσθησαν, ἢ εἰς τοὺς οἴκους, ὅπου μάρτυρες τῶν αἱρετικῶν ἐτάφησαν• πολλοὶ γὰρ καὶ ἀπὸ τοὺς αἱρετικοὺς ἐν τῷ καιρῷ τοῦ διωγμοῦ καὶ τῆς εἰδωλολατρείας μέχρι θανάτου ἐκαρτέρησαν, τοὺς ὁποίους μάρτυρας ὠνόμασαν οἱ ὁμόδοξοι αὐτῶν. Ἀλλ’ οὐδὲ οἱ ὀρθόδοξοι, λέγω, Χριστιανοὶ πρέπει νά πηγαίνουν εἰς αὐτοὺς ἡ διὰ νά προσευχηθοῦν, ἢ διὰ θεραπείαν, ἠγουν, ἢ διὰ νά τοὺς τιμήσουν, ἢ διὰ να ζητήσουν ἰατρείαν ἀπὸ αὐτοὺς εἰς τάς ἀσθενείας των. Ὅσοι δὲ τοῦτο ἠθελαν κάμῃ, διορίζει ὁ παρών Κανών νά ἀφορίζωνται πρὸς καιρόν, ἕως ὅπου νά μετανοήσουν καὶ νά ἐξομολογηθουν ὅτι ἔσφαλαν. Ὅρᾳ καὶ τὸν με΄. Ἀποστολικόν.
orientation: The Council of Laodicea is decreeing that church members must not go to the burial places or martyrs' shrines of heretics for prayer or healing, and that those who do so are to be excommunicated for a time.
pass_a_gloss: Concerning not permitting those of the church to go to the cemeteries or to the so-called martyria of all the heretics, for the sake of prayer or healing; but such persons, if they are faithful, are to become excommunicated until a certain time. And those repenting, and confessing that they have erred, are to be received back. Interpretation. Not only must the heretics not enter into the churches of the orthodox, but neither must those of the church, that is the faithful lay people and orthodox, go to the cemeteries of the heretics, where certain persons renowned among the heretics were buried, or to the houses where martyrs of the heretics were buried; for many even from the heretics in the time of persecution and of idolatry endured unto death, whom their fellow-believers named martyrs. But neither must the orthodox, I say, Christians go to them either in order to pray, or for healing, that is, either in order to honor them, or in order to seek a cure from them in their illnesses. And as many as would do this, the present canon ordains that they be excommunicated for a time, until they repent and confess that they erred. See also the 45th Apostolic canon.

choices.why: The source uses the technical term for martyr shrines; keeping it as 'martyria' preserves the specific cultic site meaning rather than a generic 'shrines'.
The glossary mandates 'excommunicated' for ἀκοινώνητος; the passive infinitive with γίνεσθαι conveys the imposed state.
rejected: are to be barred from communion
are to be out of communion

choices.why: The indefinite τινός indicates a fixed but unspecified period, matching the later interpretation's 'for a time'.
The perfect infinitive of σφάλλω expresses a completed error; 'have erred' captures the perfect aspect.
The middle/passive infinitive indicates readmission to communion after repentance, not mere acceptance.
The term means those of the same belief; 'fellow-believers' conveys the shared heretical conviction without implying orthodoxy.

pass_b_english: Those who belong to the church must not go to the cemeteries or the so-called martyria of any heretics for prayer or for healing. If any of the faithful do so, they are to become excommunicated until a certain time. But if they repent and confess that they have erred, they are to be received back.

Interpretation. Not only must heretics not enter the churches of the orthodox, but neither should those of the church—that is, the faithful laity and orthodox—go to the cemeteries of heretics, where certain persons famous among the heretics have been buried, or to the houses where martyrs of the heretics were buried. For many of the heretics also endured to the death in the time of persecution and idolatry, and their fellow-believers called them martyrs. But neither, I say, should orthodox Christians go to them either to pray or for healing—that is, either to honor them or to seek a cure from them for their illnesses. Whoever does this, the present canon decrees, is to be excommunicated for a time, until they repent and confess that they have erred. See also Apostolic Canon 45.

last_rejected.why: Greek says 'idolatry' but context demands 'paganism' or 'heathenism' as the era of persecution; heretics weren't idolaters.
last_rejected.ruling: εἰδωλολατρείας means 'idolatry'; rendering it as such is accurate, not a mistranslation.

last_rejected.why: Greek says 'those of the same opinion/sect' (fellow-heretics), not 'fellow-believers' which implies legitimate belief.
last_rejected.ruling: ὁμόδοξοι means 'like-minded/same-opinion'; 'fellow-believers' is within normal range, not misleading.
